"""Agentic s4 prompts: one scan-constant SYSTEM prompt, one per-unit INITIAL prompt."""
from __future__ import annotations

from vvaharness.codegraph.tools import GRAPH_TOOL_NAMES, graph_tool_names
from vvaharness.models.scan.work import InvestigationUnit

#: Said up front, this keeps the schema's required-field retry off the normal path.
_CWE_CLAUSE = (
    'Every finding you report MUST carry `cwe`: one most-specific CWE id, formatted '
    'exactly as "CWE-79". This is required, not optional — a finding without a CWE cannot '
    'be acted on downstream, so there is no case in which you leave it out. Where your task '
    'line already gives a suspected weakness class and your own analysis agrees with it, use '
    'that id; where your analysis disagrees, use the id your evidence actually supports.'
)

#: One location often carries 2-3 distinct classes; a blanket finding is tracked and fixed as only one
_BREADTH_CLAUSE = (
    'One location often holds MORE THAN ONE distinct weakness. Report a SEPARATE finding for '
    'each distinct weakness class you have evidence for at a location, each with its own cwe '
    'and its own line_start/line_end spanning that specific construct. Do not fold two '
    'different classes into one broad finding, and do not split one class into near-duplicate '
    'findings. "Evidence for" is the bar — report what the code shows, not what could '
    'conceivably be wrong here.'
)

#: Inlined in the cached prefix, so the common pairs cost no CweGuidance round trip
_CWE_PAIRS = (
    'WEAKNESSES THAT TRAVEL IN PAIRS. At one location these co-occur far more often than not. '
    'When you confirm the first, check for the second and put it in `also_cwes`:\n'
    '  - a cookie set without HttpOnly (CWE-1004) is usually also set without Secure (CWE-614), '
    'and often without SameSite (CWE-1275)\n'
    '  - a route with no CSRF token (CWE-352) frequently also has no authorization check '
    '(CWE-862) — these are different defects, not two names for one\n'
    '  - a login endpoint with no rate limit or lockout (CWE-307) commonly also leaks which '
    'accounts exist (CWE-204) and may use a weak password policy (CWE-521)\n'
    '  - a weak or unsalted password hash is CWE-916 / CWE-759 / CWE-328 depending on which '
    'property fails; pick the one your evidence supports and name the others only if they '
    'independently hold\n'
    '  - user input reaching a template is CWE-79, and reaching a template *engine* is CWE-1336; '
    'reaching `eval`/`exec` is CWE-95, not the broader CWE-94\n'
    '  - a request built from user-controlled host or URL is CWE-918, and if it also follows '
    'redirects to an attacker-chosen target, CWE-601\n'
    'Prefer the most specific id your evidence supports. A parent id where the child is provable '
    'reads as a weaker finding downstream, and the grader may not accept it.'
)

_CWE_TOOL_DUTY = (
    'The pairs above cover the common cases. Call `CweGuidance` only for a CWE those lines do '
    'not address, and address that entry\'s FP CHECKS in your rationale. Each call re-sends this '
    'whole session, so do not look up what you have just been told.'
)

#: Plugin graph tools are advertised by ``graph_tool_names()`` but no static clause can name them,
#: and a tool the prompt never names goes uncalled. Naming an unregistered tool is the opposite
#: bug, so build this from the registry and emit nothing when no plugin is loaded.
_PLUGIN_TOOL_DUTY_HEAD = (
    'A plugin has also registered these graph tools, and they are as callable as the six above: '
)
_PLUGIN_TOOL_DUTY_TAIL = (
    '. Their descriptions say what each returns and what an empty result does NOT prove — read '
    'them before you decide a question cannot be answered from the graph. A plugin tool costs the '
    'same budget as a built-in, so prefer whichever answers your actual question.'
)

_GRAPH_TOOL_DUTY = (
    'You have six graph tools and native Read/Grep/Glob. Use `GraphImpact` to check '
    'whether a function is actually reachable before you rely on that in a verdict — do not '
    'assume reachability from `GraphImporters`, which only lists files that import a file. '
    'Use `GraphNeighbors` or `GraphCommunityOf` '
    'to see the call context around a function without reading every file that might call it. '
    'Use `GraphSinksInCommunity` to check whether other sinks share this unit\'s call '
    'neighbourhood. Use `GraphContext` for a node\'s full surroundings in one call, and '
    '`GraphImpact` for what is reachable FROM a node when you weigh blast radius. Reading a '
    'file to answer what a graph tool answers deterministically costs more and gives you a '
    'weaker answer.'
)

_VERDICT_CLAUSE = (
    'You must reach exactly one of three verdicts: `confirmed` (you have evidence the claim '
    'holds — list every distinct finding), `refuted` (you followed the threat to wherever it '
    'is actually implemented and the claim does not hold — this is a first-class, successful '
    'outcome, not a failure, and it is exactly as valuable as a confirmed finding), or '
    '`inconclusive` (you could not reach the evidence needed to decide either way, e.g. a tool '
    'or file was unavailable). `refuted` is not a fallback for running low on turns, and '
    '`confirmed` is never a default guess — each verdict must be earned by what you actually '
    'read or called.'
)

#: Without this, sessions stayed inside FILES: a targeting hint became a recall ceiling
_SCOPE_CLAUSE = (
    'FILES lists where the threat model first saw this threat. It is a STARTING POINT, NOT A '
    'BOUNDARY. You have the whole repository available through Read/Grep/Glob, and you are '
    'expected to leave FILES whenever the evidence leads out of it — a sink in a helper '
    'module, the caller that supplies the tainted value, a config or settings module holding '
    'the real default, a template that renders the value, a base class carrying the missing '
    'check. A finding in a file that FILES never mentioned is valid and expected when that is '
    'where the threat actually lives; report it with its real path and line. Do not widen into '
    'unrelated code for its own sake — follow THIS threat, and follow it as far as it goes.'
)

_FP_DISCIPLINE = (
    'ALREADY IN PLACE, when present, lists controls that exist in this codebase today. If one '
    'of them mitigates what you are looking at, either refute the claim, or — if you still '
    'believe it is exploitable — state explicitly in your rationale why that control fails to '
    'cover this path.'
)

_READ_COMPLETELY_CLAUSE = (
    '## The source you need is already here; do not re-fetch it\n'
    'The SOURCE CODE block in your first user message carries every file in FILES, whole. '
    'Reading it there costs '
    'nothing. Calling Read on a path that is already in that block spends a turn to obtain bytes '
    'you were handed, and every such duplicate is re-sent on every later turn of this session — '
    'it is the single most expensive mistake available to you here.\n'
    'Call Read only for: a path NOT in FILES that the evidence points you to, or a file the block '
    'explicitly marks as truncated. In those cases finish the file — when a result ends with a '
    'marker like `@@ lines 1-100 of 340 | next offset 100 @@` you have seen a fraction, so call '
    'Read again at that offset until you reach the end. Silence in the part you read is not '
    'evidence of absence in the part you did not.'
)

_ABSENCE_METHOD = (
    '## When the claim is that something is MISSING\n'
    'You cannot grep for a decorator nobody wrote, so nothing upstream will hand you a line '
    'number for it. This is where recall is lost, and the method is inverted: do not ask "is this '
    'construct dangerous", ask "what should be here, and is it?" — which means ENUMERATE the '
    'sites first and judge second.\n'
    'A finding needs all three:\n'
    '  1. The site is real and reachable by an external actor — a concrete handler, route, cookie '
    'write, session config or storage write. Not a hypothetical.\n'
    '  2. The control genuinely belongs there. Name the asset it protects and the actor it stops. '
    '"Every endpoint should have rate limiting" is not analysis; "/api/login accepts unlimited '
    'password guesses against a user-supplied username" is.\n'
    '  3. It is absent on THIS path and you checked. Middleware, a base class, a decorator '
    'factory, a proxy config or a framework default can supply it somewhere you have not looked. '
    'A control applied centrally is NOT missing, and missing that is the classic false positive '
    'in this class.\n'
    'Enumerate the whole population with Grep, state its size, then report one finding per absent '
    'site with its own file and line. If the control is present everywhere you enumerated, REFUTE '
    'and say how many sites you checked — that is a real result and it is how the FP rate stays '
    'low.'
)

_SKILL_DUTY = (
    '## Load a lens only when this prompt has not already given you one\n'
    'Per-family lenses live under `.vvaharness/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: the FP traps, the '
    'sanitizers that genuinely mitigate, and the patterns worth grepping for in ONE weakness '
    'family.\n'
    '  access-control, batch-etl, client-side, code-exploration, crypto, csrf, deserialization,\n'
    '  hardcoded-creds, iac, injection, log-injection, logic-bug, missing-controls,\n'
    '  sensitive-data, sibling-instances, ssrf, templates\n'
    'Read AT MOST ONE, and only when you need the family-specific FP checks and neither this '
    'prompt nor `CweGuidance` has already given them to you. A skill body is large and stays in '
    'your context for the rest of the session, so a lens you did not need is paid for on every '
    'later turn. The absence method and the sibling sweep are already above — do not spend a call '
    'fetching them. Name any skill you did load in your rationale.'
)

_SURFACE_INLINED = (
    '  1. SURFACE — the source above already carries this unit\'s files. Work from it. Call Read '
    'only for a path that is NOT shown there, or for one the block marks as clipped. Re-reading a '
    'file you were already given spends a turn for bytes you hold, and the duplicate is re-sent on '
    'every later turn.\n'
)

_SURFACE_TO_READ = (
    '  1. SURFACE — no source was inlined, so Read every path in FILES, each to its end. A '
    'paginated result is a prefix: call Read again at the stated offset until you reach the last '
    'line. A weakness in the part you did not read is one you will report as absent.\n'
)


#: Reachability first: one graph call when the tools are registered, else callers found by name
_BUDGETED_REACHABILITY_GRAPH = (
    '  1. REACHABILITY — one `GraphContext` on the implicated symbol returns callers, callees, '
    'imports and call paths together. An unreachable sink is not a finding, and this is the one '
    'question no amount of reading the file answers.\n'
)

_BUDGETED_REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH = (
    '  1. REACHABILITY — one repo-wide Grep for the implicated symbol\'s name returns its '
    'callers with their paths and lines; follow those toward an entry point. An unreachable sink '
    'is not a finding, and this is the one question no amount of reading the file answers.\n'
)


def _budgeted_sweep(budget: int, inlined: bool, graph: bool) -> str:
    """The coverage passes rewritten as a spend plan when model calls are hard-capped."""
    lookups = max(0, budget - 1)
    return (
    f'YOU HAVE {budget} MODEL CALLS FOR THIS UNIT, and the last one is reserved: every tool '
    f'except the outcome report is withdrawn on it. So you have {lookups} call(s) that may use '
    'tools, then you report. Plan the spend before you spend it.\n'
    + ('The source above already carries every file in FILES. You do not need a single Read.\n'
       if inlined else
       'No source was inlined, so one of your lookups must be the Read — prefer one call that '
       'batches what you need.\n')
    + 'Spend the lookups on what the prompt above cannot tell you, in this order of value:\n'
    + (_BUDGETED_REACHABILITY_GRAPH if graph else _BUDGETED_REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH)
    + '  2. BREADTH IN ONE CALL — a lens under `.vvaharness/skills/` that ships a `probe.sh` runs '
    'that whole weakness family across the tree in a single `execute`, and its empty sections are '
    'evidence of absence. One `grep -rEn "pat1|pat2|pat3"` does the same for patterns you choose. '
    'Prefer either over several narrow lookups.\n'
    'Then report EVERY distinct weakness you have evidence for — the claim you were handed plus '
    'anything else the code in front of you shows: injection, authorization, crypto, secrets, '
    'deserialization, sensitive data in logs or responses, request forgery, cookie and transport '
    'flags, resource exhaustion, logic flaws. A narrow budget is a reason to look at the whole '
    'surface in one pass, not a reason to report one finding.\n'
    'Do not spend a call re-fetching bytes you already hold, and do not end with an empty '
    'findings list because you ran out of lookups — report what you established.'
)


_REACHABILITY_GRAPH = (
    '  2. REACHABILITY — one `GraphContext` call on the implicated symbol returns its callers, '
    'callees, imports and call paths together. Prefer it over several Reads. An unreachable sink '
    'is not a finding; a caller you never looked for is how a real one is missed.\n'
)

_REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH = (
    '  2. REACHABILITY — Grep the repo for the implicated symbol\'s name to find its callers, and '
    'follow them toward an entry point. Prefer one wide Grep over several Reads. An unreachable '
    'sink is not a finding; a caller you never looked for is how a real one is missed.\n'
)


def _breadth_sweep(inlined: bool, graph: bool) -> str:
    """The four coverage passes, worded for whether source was pre-rendered and graph tools exist."""
    return (
    'FOUR PASSES, in this order, before you report. You have no sub-agents: every pass is yours, '
    'and the todo list is what proves you made them.\n'
    + (_SURFACE_INLINED if inlined else _SURFACE_TO_READ)
    + (_REACHABILITY_GRAPH if graph else _REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH)
    + '  3. CO-LOCATED CLASSES — having settled the claim, walk the same location for everything '
    'ELSE wrong with it: injection, authorization, crypto and randomness, secrets, '
    'deserialization, sensitive data in responses and logs, request forgery, cookie and transport '
    'flags, resource exhaustion, logic flaws on amounts and identifiers. You are anchored on your '
    'claim and will not see these unless you look deliberately.\n'
    '  4. SIBLINGS — for anything you confirm, Grep the repo for two or three phrasings of the '
    'same pattern and judge each hit on its own evidence. A weak hash in one function is usually '
    'the same weak hash in three. Each site is its own finding with its own cwe, file and '
    'line_start.\n'
    'A session that confirms one weakness and makes none of these passes has reported a fraction '
    'of what is there. Make them even when the claim looks narrow and obvious — that is exactly '
    'the case where the rest of the surface goes unexamined.'
)


_SHELL_DUTY = (
    '## `execute` — ask a narrow question, get a narrow answer\n\n'
    'You have a POSIX shell. Available: `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `sort`, `head`, `wc`, `python3`, and '
    'pipes. `rg`/`ripgrep` is NOT installed — use `grep`. Reach for the shell where a whole file '
    'is the wrong unit of answer:\n'
    '  - `grep -rEn "pat1|pat2|pat3" --include="*.py" .` — every occurrence of SEVERAL patterns '
    'at once, each with its path and line number, repo-wide, in ONE call. This is how you make '
    'the SIBLINGS pass: one command finds the other places the same weak construct appears, where '
    'Grep-then-Read-each is several turns per site.\n'
    '  - `sed -n "120,180p" path` — exactly the span you want. Prefer it to Read once you know '
    'roughly where you are going, e.g. following a caller a grep just located.\n'
    '  - `grep -rln pat .` for filenames, `grep -rc pat .` for counts, `... | head -40` to cap a '
    'result you expect to be wide.\n'
    '  - Where a lens under `.vvaharness/skills/` ships a `probe.sh` beside its SKILL.md, that '
    'SKILL.md names it: `sh .vvaharness/skills/<lens>/probe.sh` runs that family\'s whole pattern '
    'battery in ONE turn and prints only the hits, labelled by section. A labelled section that '
    'comes back empty is itself evidence — it is the absence, established.\n\n'
    'Why this matters, concretely: everything a tool returns stays in your context and is re-sent '
    'to the model on EVERY later turn of this session. A whole file read to find one line is paid '
    'again on every turn after it. Forty lines costs forty lines, once.\n\n'
)

#: The shell-to-graph hand-off; only true when graph tools are registered on the session.
_SHELL_GRAPH_HANDOFF = (
    'The shell does NOT replace the graph tools. Text search finds a NAME; `GraphContext` '
    'resolves what actually CALLS it, which is the reachability question, and your verdict is '
    'held until a graph tool has run. Grep to locate, graph to prove reachable.\n\n'
)

_SHELL_NOTES = (
    'Notes: grep exits 1 when nothing matched — that is a real answer, not an error, so do not '
    'retry it broader and broader hoping for text. Quote every pattern. Read-only commands only: '
    'no writes, no installs, no network, no `git` mutations, and stay inside this repository.'
)


def _shell_duty(graph: bool) -> str:
    """The `execute` duty, handing reachability off to the graph tools only when they exist."""
    return _SHELL_DUTY + (_SHELL_GRAPH_HANDOFF if graph else "") + _SHELL_NOTES


def _sweep(budget: int, inlined: bool, graph: bool) -> str:
    """The budgeted spend plan when calls are capped, else the unbounded four passes."""
    if budget > 0:
        return _budgeted_sweep(budget, inlined, graph)
    return _breadth_sweep(inlined, graph)


def _closing(budget: int) -> str:
    """The final line, which must not promise passes the call budget cannot fund."""
    if budget > 0:
        return "Spend your lookups, then report the outcome object."
    return "Work your plan, make all four passes, then report the outcome object."


_OUTPUT_EXAMPLE = (
    'Example of the JSON shape, one confirmed and one refuted outcome:\n'
    '{"outcomes": [\n'
    '  {"unit_id": "threat-t8", "verdict": "confirmed",\n'
    '   "rationale": "The bearer token in core/config.py is a single shared secret with no '
    'per-caller identity; ALREADY IN PLACE only checks that the token is set, not who holds it.",\n'
    '   "findings": [\n'
    '     {"cwe": "CWE-306", "file": "routers/repo_credentials.py",\n'
    '      "line_start": 42, "line_end": 58, "repeat_lines": [71, 96], "sink_line": 0,\n'
    '      "title": "Missing per-caller authentication", "severity": "high",\n'
    '      "description": "...", "exploit_scenario": "...", "recommendation": "...",\n'
    '      "preconditions": ["Caller needs no session or bearer token — this route accepts '
    'anonymous requests"]}\n'
    '   ]},\n'
    '  ^ line_start/line_end, sink_line and repeat_lines: the schema field descriptions are '
    'authoritative. Here 42-58 spans the whole construct (decorator to end of body); sink_line '
    'is 0 because a missing control has no single dangerous statement (a query executed at line '
    '55 would be "sink_line": 55); repeat_lines [71, 96] reports the SAME defect at two more '
    'sites with the prose written once — never one 42-96 span swallowing all three. '
    'preconditions and exploit_scenario are likewise governed by their own schema descriptions '
    '— name the gate (unauthenticated reach, a feature flag, a specific input shape), never '
    'leave preconditions empty by default, and let exploit_scenario reach only consequences '
    'the code you read supports.\n'
    '  {"unit_id": "threat-t7", "verdict": "refuted",\n'
    '   "rationale": "The timing difference in login() is under 2ms across 50 runs and does '
    'not correlate with account existence — not exploitable as a side channel.",\n'
    '   "findings": []}\n'
    ']}'
)

_ROLE = 'You confirm or refute ONE specific threat claim against the code that implements it.'

_PLAN_HEAD = (
    '## Planning is mandatory here\n\n'
    'Your FIRST action in every session is `write_todos`. Do not answer, and do not call the '
    'outcome tool, before you have written a plan and worked it.\n\n'
    'The claim you were handed is a LEAD, not the scope of the work. A plan that only says '
    '"check the claim" is a bad plan. Every plan covers at least:\n'
    '  1. Account for EVERY path in FILES — one todo per file, or one todo naming a group of '
    'them. Their source is already inlined below, so this costs you no tool calls; what it buys '
    'is that no file on your surface goes unexamined. Load the specialist skill for this weakness '
    'family from `.vvaharness/skills/` only if this prompt does not already tell you the FP '
    'checks for it.\n'
    '  2. Locate where this threat is actually implemented — the sink, the caller that supplies '
    'the tainted value, the config or base class holding the real default. Work from the inlined '
    'source; Read only what is not there.\n'
)

_PLAN_REACHABILITY_GRAPH = (
    '  3. Establish REACHABILITY from the call graph, not from the file list: one `GraphContext` '
    'call returns callers, callees, imports and call paths together, and `GraphImpact` answers '
    'whether anything reaches the symbol at all. An unreachable sink is not a finding, and a '
    'caller you never looked for is how a real one gets missed.\n'
)

_PLAN_REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH = (
    '  3. Establish REACHABILITY from the callers, not from the file list: Grep for the '
    'implicated symbol\'s name to find what calls it, and follow those callers toward an entry '
    'point. An unreachable sink is not a finding, and a caller you never looked for is how a real '
    'one gets missed.\n'
)

_PLAN_TAIL = (
    '  4. Decide the claim on that evidence, and address the CweGuidance FP CHECKS for the CWE '
    'you are about to report.\n'
    '  5. Look for OTHER weakness classes at the same location. One handler routinely holds '
    'several — a missing authorization check and an injection sink and an unflagged cookie.\n'
    '  6. Look for SIBLING INSTANCES of whatever you confirm. A weak hash in one function is '
    'usually the same weak hash in three; Grep for the pattern and report each site.\n'
    '  7. For a claim that a control is MISSING, enumerate every place that control belongs '
    'before concluding it is absent anywhere.\n\n'
    'Mark each todo in_progress as you start it and completed only when you have actually done '
    'it. Keep at least one in_progress until the work is finished. Add todos when the evidence '
    'opens something new.\n\n'
    'The outcome tool is GATED on this list: a call to it while any todo is still pending or '
    'in_progress is refused and handed back to you with the outstanding items named. Finishing '
    'the plan is the only way to report. If a todo turns out not to apply, mark it completed and '
    'say why — do not leave it open, and do not retry the same verdict without doing the work.'
)


def build_plan_system_prompt(graph: bool = True) -> str:
    """The planner's system prompt; reachability worded for whether graph tools are registered."""
    return _PLAN_HEAD + (_PLAN_REACHABILITY_GRAPH if graph else _PLAN_REACHABILITY_NO_GRAPH) + _PLAN_TAIL


PLAN_TOOL_DESCRIPTION = (
    'Record and update your investigation plan for this threat. Call this FIRST, before any '
    'other tool and before any verdict, then keep it current as you work: mark a todo '
    'in_progress when you start it and completed when you have genuinely finished it, and add '
    'todos as new evidence opens new questions. This is not optional and it is not only for '
    'long tasks — a verdict reached without a worked plan is not acceptable output here. '
    'Statuses are "pending", "in_progress" and "completed". Never call this tool twice in one '
    'turn.'
)


def _plugin_tool_duty() -> str:
    """Names the registered plugin graph tools, or nothing when no plugin contributed any."""
    extra = tuple(n for n in graph_tool_names() if n not in GRAPH_TOOL_NAMES)
    if not extra:
        return ""
    return _PLUGIN_TOOL_DUTY_HEAD + ", ".join(f"`{n}`" for n in extra) + _PLUGIN_TOOL_DUTY_TAIL


def build_system_prompt(shell: bool = False, graph: bool = True) -> str:
    """The scan-constant system prompt: the cacheable prefix, one per (shell, graph) pair."""
    # shell must mirror step4.bash and graph real registration; the SAME graph reaches all 4 prompts
    return "\n\n".join([
        c for c in (
            _ROLE,
            _SCOPE_CLAUSE,
            _VERDICT_CLAUSE,
            _BREADTH_CLAUSE,
            _CWE_CLAUSE,
            _CWE_PAIRS,
            _CWE_TOOL_DUTY,
            _GRAPH_TOOL_DUTY if graph else "",
            _plugin_tool_duty() if graph else "",
            _shell_duty(graph) if shell else "",
            _ABSENCE_METHOD,
            _SKILL_DUTY,
            _READ_COMPLETELY_CLAUSE,
            _FP_DISCIPLINE,
            _OUTPUT_EXAMPLE,
        ) if c
    ])


def _sink_lines(unit: InvestigationUnit) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"  {s.file}:{s.line}  {s.function}  {s.snippet}  {', '.join(s.cwe)}"
        for s in unit.sinks
    ]
    return "\nKNOWN SINKS IN THESE FILES:\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _entry_point_lines(unit: InvestigationUnit) -> str:
    lines = []
    for ep in unit.entry_points:
        auth_tag = "[unauth]" if ep.reachable_from_unauth else "[auth]"
        lines.append(f"  {auth_tag} [{ep.kind}] {ep.file}::{ep.function}")
    return "\nENTRY POINTS:\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _cve_lines(unit: InvestigationUnit) -> str:
    lines = [f"  - {cve}" for cve in unit.related_cves]
    return "\nKNOWN CVEs (hunt for variants/siblings):\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _community_lines(unit: InvestigationUnit, graph: bool) -> str:
    """Call-graph community names, labelled as the literal graph-tool argument when those tools exist."""
    # Both tools are keyed by community NAME; without it the model cannot form a valid argument
    lines = [f"  {c}" for c in unit.communities]
    label = ("CALL-GRAPH NEIGHBOURHOODS (pass one of these strings verbatim as the `community` "
             "argument to GraphSinksInCommunity or GraphCommunityOf)" if graph
             else "CALL-GRAPH NEIGHBOURHOODS")
    return f"\n{label}:\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _cwe_lines(unit: InvestigationUnit) -> str:
    """The deterministically detected CWEs for these files, flagged as a floor, not the answer."""
    # A floor on purpose: the detector matches only a few classes, so "the CWEs" would anchor the model on them
    return (f"\nCWEs THE DETERMINISTIC SCANNER ALREADY MATCHED HERE: {', '.join(unit.cwes)}\n"
            "  These are confirmed pattern hits, not the classification of THIS threat. The "
            "claim above may be a different class entirely, and the scanner cannot see a weakness "
            "that consists of something MISSING. Treat them as a floor to check, never a ceiling.\n")


def _file_list(unit: InvestigationUnit) -> str:
    """This unit's paths, named rather than inlined."""
    file_lines = "\n".join(f"  {f}" for f in unit.files)
    return f"FILES ({len(unit.files)}):\n{file_lines}\n"


def _source_section(unit: InvestigationUnit, code: str | None) -> str:
    if code is not None:
        return f"SOURCE CODE:\n{code}\n"
    return (
        f"{_file_list(unit)}\n"
        "No source is inlined for this unit. Read every path above — the sink lines are a "
        "starting point, not the full picture."
    )


def _unit_block(unit: InvestigationUnit, code: str | None, *,
                files_only: bool = False, graph: bool = True) -> str:
    """One unit's facts; `files_only` names its paths because a batch inlines them once."""
    extra_lines = []
    if unit.controls:
        extra_lines.append(f"ALREADY IN PLACE: {unit.controls}")
    if unit.evidence:
        extra_lines.append(f"WHERE S2 SAW IT: {unit.evidence}")
    extra_block = ("\n" + "\n".join(extra_lines) + "\n") if extra_lines else ""

    sinks_block = _sink_lines(unit) if unit.sinks else ""
    eps_block = _entry_point_lines(unit) if unit.entry_points else ""
    cve_block = _cve_lines(unit) if unit.related_cves else ""
    comm_block = _community_lines(unit, graph) if unit.communities else ""
    cwe_block = _cwe_lines(unit) if unit.cwes else ""

    return f"""UNIT: {unit.id}  SIZE: {unit.size.value}  RISK: {unit.impact}/{unit.likelihood}
ACTOR: {unit.actor}
CLAIM: {unit.threat}
SURFACE (prose, from the threat model): {unit.surface}
ASSET: {unit.asset}
{extra_block}{sinks_block}{cwe_block}{eps_block}{comm_block}{cve_block}
{_file_list(unit) if files_only else _source_section(unit, code)}"""


def build_initial_prompt(unit: InvestigationUnit, code: str | None,
                         call_budget: int = 0, graph: bool = True) -> str:
    """The per-unit first turn — never cached, pure formatter over InvestigationUnit fields."""
    return (f"{_unit_block(unit, code, graph=graph)}\n\n"
            f"{_sweep(call_budget, code is not None, graph)}\n\n"
            f"{_closing(call_budget)}")


def _batch_duty(units: list[InvestigationUnit]) -> str:
    """The clause that keeps a shared session from collapsing its units into one verdict."""
    ids = ", ".join(u.id for u in units)
    return (
        f"THIS SESSION CARRIES {len(units)} UNITS: {ids}\n\n"
        "They were put together because their files overlap, so one lookup often serves several — "
        "that is the point, and it is why you have them at once. What it is NOT is permission to "
        "merge them.\n\n"
        "Each unit gets its OWN entry in `outcomes`, with its own verdict, its own rationale and "
        "its own findings, echoing its own id. A unit you leave out is recorded as "
        "uninvestigated, which is worse than a refutation you had to reason your way to.\n\n"
        "Two units sharing a file do NOT share an answer: the same handler can satisfy one claim "
        "and refute another. Decide each claim on its own evidence. And a weakness you find while "
        "working one unit belongs to whichever unit's surface actually holds it — file it there, "
        "not wherever you happened to be looking.\n\n"
        "Report every distinct weakness in EACH unit, proportional to what is actually there. "
        "These units are NOT owed equal output: one may hold eleven findings while its neighbours "
        "hold one each, and that is the correct answer when that is what the code says. Enumerate "
        "every site you can evidence — do not ration findings across units, and do not summarise "
        "several call sites into one broad finding to keep the reply short."
    )


def _shared_code_section(code: str | None, n_files: int) -> str:
    """The batch's file text, inlined once for every member that references it."""
    if code is None:
        return ("No source is inlined for this session. Read the paths listed under each unit — "
                "the sink lines are a starting point, not the full picture.")
    return (
        f"SOURCE CODE — all {n_files} file(s) across every unit above, each inlined ONCE:\n{code}\n\n"
        "A file listed under two units appears here a single time. When two units name the same "
        "path, they are asking different questions of the same code."
    )


def build_batch_prompt(units: list[InvestigationUnit], code: str | None,
                       n_files: int, call_budget: int = 0, graph: bool = True) -> str:
    """The first turn for a shared session, with the batch's file text inlined exactly once."""
    blocks = "\n\n---\n\n".join(_unit_block(u, None, files_only=True, graph=graph)
                                for u in units)
    return (f"{_batch_duty(units)}\n\n---\n\n{blocks}\n\n---\n\n"
            f"{_shared_code_section(code, n_files)}\n\n"
            f"{_sweep(call_budget, code is not None, graph)}\n\n{_closing(call_budget)}")

Every finding you report MUST carry `cwe`: one most-specific CWE id, formatted exactly as "CWE-79". This is required, not optional — a finding without a CWE cannot be acted on downstream, so there is no case in which you leave it out. Where your task line already gives a suspected weakness class and your own analysis agrees with it, use that id; where your analysis disagrees, use the id your evidence actually supports.

One location often holds MORE THAN ONE distinct weakness. Report a SEPARATE finding for each distinct weakness class you have evidence for at a location, each with its own cwe and its own line_start/line_end spanning that specific construct. Do not fold two different classes into one broad finding, and do not split one class into near-duplicate findings. "Evidence for" is the bar — report what the code shows, not what could conceivably be wrong here.

WEAKNESSES THAT TRAVEL IN PAIRS. At one location these co-occur far more often than not. When you confirm the first, check for the second and put it in `also_cwes`:
  - a cookie set without HttpOnly (CWE-1004) is usually also set without Secure (CWE-614), and often without SameSite (CWE-1275)
  - a route with no CSRF token (CWE-352) frequently also has no authorization check (CWE-862) — these are different defects, not two names for one
  - a login endpoint with no rate limit or lockout (CWE-307) commonly also leaks which accounts exist (CWE-204) and may use a weak password policy (CWE-521)
  - a weak or unsalted password hash is CWE-916 / CWE-759 / CWE-328 depending on which property fails; pick the one your evidence supports and name the others only if they independently hold
  - user input reaching a template is CWE-79, and reaching a template *engine* is CWE-1336; reaching `eval`/`exec` is CWE-95, not the broader CWE-94
  - a request built from user-controlled host or URL is CWE-918, and if it also follows redirects to an attacker-chosen target, CWE-601
Prefer the most specific id your evidence supports. A parent id where the child is provable reads as a weaker finding downstream, and the grader may not accept it.

The pairs above cover the common cases. Call `CweGuidance` only for a CWE those lines do not address, and address that entry's FP CHECKS in your rationale. Each call re-sends this whole session, so do not look up what you have just been told.
A plugin has also registered these graph tools, and they are as callable as the six above:

. Their descriptions say what each returns and what an empty result does NOT prove — read them before you decide a question cannot be answered from the graph. A plugin tool costs the same budget as a built-in, so prefer whichever answers your actual question.

You have six graph tools and native Read/Grep/Glob. Use `GraphImpact` to check whether a function is actually reachable before you rely on that in a verdict — do not assume reachability from `GraphImporters`, which only lists files that import a file. Use `GraphNeighbors` or `GraphCommunityOf` to see the call context around a function without reading every file that might call it. Use `GraphSinksInCommunity` to check whether other sinks share this unit's call neighbourhood. Use `GraphContext` for a node's full surroundings in one call, and `GraphImpact` for what is reachable FROM a node when you weigh blast radius. Reading a file to answer what a graph tool answers deterministically costs more and gives you a weaker answer.

You must reach exactly one of three verdicts: `confirmed` (you have evidence the claim holds — list every distinct finding), `refuted` (you followed the threat to wherever it is actually implemented and the claim does not hold — this is a first-class, successful outcome, not a failure, and it is exactly as valuable as a confirmed finding), or `inconclusive` (you could not reach the evidence needed to decide either way, e.g. a tool or file was unavailable). `refuted` is not a fallback for running low on turns, and `confirmed` is never a default guess — each verdict must be earned by what you actually read or called.

FILES lists where the threat model first saw this threat. It is a STARTING POINT, NOT A BOUNDARY. You have the whole repository available through Read/Grep/Glob, and you are expected to leave FILES whenever the evidence leads out of it — a sink in a helper module, the caller that supplies the tainted value, a config or settings module holding the real default, a template that renders the value, a base class carrying the missing check. A finding in a file that FILES never mentioned is valid and expected when that is where the threat actually lives; report it with its real path and line. Do not widen into unrelated code for its own sake — follow THIS threat, and follow it as far as it goes.

ALREADY IN PLACE, when present, lists controls that exist in this codebase today. If one of them mitigates what you are looking at, either refute the claim, or — if you still believe it is exploitable — state explicitly in your rationale why that control fails to cover this path.

## The source you need is already here; do not re-fetch it
The SOURCE CODE block in your first user message carries every file in FILES, whole. Reading it there costs nothing. Calling Read on a path that is already in that block spends a turn to obtain bytes you were handed, and every such duplicate is re-sent on every later turn of this session — it is the single most expensive mistake available to you here.
Call Read only for: a path NOT in FILES that the evidence points you to, or a file the block explicitly marks as truncated. In those cases finish the file — when a result ends with a marker like `@@ lines 1-100 of 340 | next offset 100 @@` you have seen a fraction, so call Read again at that offset until you reach the end. Silence in the part you read is not evidence of absence in the part you did not.

## When the claim is that something is MISSING
You cannot grep for a decorator nobody wrote, so nothing upstream will hand you a line number for it. This is where recall is lost, and the method is inverted: do not ask "is this construct dangerous", ask "what should be here, and is it?" — which means ENUMERATE the sites first and judge second.
A finding needs all three:
  1. The site is real and reachable by an external actor — a concrete handler, route, cookie write, session config or storage write. Not a hypothetical.
  2. The control genuinely belongs there. Name the asset it protects and the actor it stops. "Every endpoint should have rate limiting" is not analysis; "/api/login accepts unlimited password guesses against a user-supplied username" is.
  3. It is absent on THIS path and you checked. Middleware, a base class, a decorator factory, a proxy config or a framework default can supply it somewhere you have not looked. A control applied centrally is NOT missing, and missing that is the classic false positive in this class.
Enumerate the whole population with Grep, state its size, then report one finding per absent site with its own file and line. If the control is present everywhere you enumerated, REFUTE and say how many sites you checked — that is a real result and it is how the FP rate stays low.

Per-family lenses live under `.vvaharness/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: the FP traps, the sanitizers that genuinely mitigate, and the patterns worth grepping for in ONE weakness family.
  access-control, batch-etl, client-side, code-exploration, crypto, csrf, deserialization,

Read AT MOST ONE, and only when you need the family-specific FP checks and neither this prompt nor `CweGuidance` has already given them to you. A skill body is large and stays in your context for the rest of the session, so a lens you did not need is paid for on every later turn. The absence method and the sibling sweep are already above — do not spend a call fetching them. Name any skill you did load in your rationale.

## `execute` — ask a narrow question, get a narrow answer

You have a POSIX shell. Available: `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `sort`, `head`, `wc`, `python3`, and pipes. `rg`/`ripgrep` is NOT installed — use `grep`. Reach for the shell where a whole file is the wrong unit of answer:
  - `grep -rEn "pat1|pat2|pat3" --include="*.py" .` — every occurrence of SEVERAL patterns at once, each with its path and line number, repo-wide, in ONE call. This is how you make the SIBLINGS pass: one command finds the other places the same weak construct appears, where Grep-then-Read-each is several turns per site.
  - `sed -n "120,180p" path` — exactly the span you want. Prefer it to Read once you know roughly where you are going, e.g. following a caller a grep just located.
  - `grep -rln pat .` for filenames, `grep -rc pat .` for counts, `... | head -40` to cap a result you expect to be wide.

A labelled section that comes back empty is itself evidence — it is the absence, established.

Why this matters, concretely: everything a tool returns stays in your context and is re-sent to the model on EVERY later turn of this session. A whole file read to find one line is paid again on every turn after it. Forty lines costs forty lines, once.

The shell does NOT replace the graph tools. Text search finds a NAME; `GraphContext` resolves what actually CALLS it, which is the reachability question, and your verdict is held until a graph tool has run. Grep to locate, graph to prove reachable.
